summary: Discovery for Dedicated GPU capacity: AstraPay needs reserved GPUs for production inference with strong isolation and burst capacity. Main concerns are predictable latency, cost controls, and security (SOC2, KMS, VPC). Next steps: pricing, security docs, technical deep dive.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-26
Time: 16:00 PT
Duration: 45m
Attendees: Samir (Redwood AE), Lena (Redwood SE), Maya (AstraPay Head of ML), Roberto (Infra Lead), Priya (PM)

00:00 Samir: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — Samir from Redwood, i'm the AE on the account, with lena our solutions engineer. how's everyone doing?
00:06 Maya: good thanks, excited to dig in, we been evaluating options for inference infra.
00:10 Roberto: yup, short on time so we'll try to keep it focused, thanks.
00:15 Samir: great, quick agenda — understand your current stack and constraints, volume and latency needs, security and isolation requirements, then talk Dedicated vs Hosted and burst/scale approach. sound good?
00:26 Priya: yup, perfect.
00:30 Lena: quick clarifying q, when you say "inference" are we talking mainly chat/generation endpoints or embeddings or both?
00:36 Maya: both but in prod it's mostly low-latency text generation for our payments customer support assistant, embeddings for search are lower qps but still important.
00:45 Lena: got it, do you have any rough qps numbers or token rates?
00:50 Maya: during peak support windows we see about 80-120 concurrent user sessions, average request is ~120 tokens out, 30 tokens in. so ballpark 200-300 qps? that's an estimate.
01:05 Roberto: and we need p95 latency under 500ms for the assistant, ideally 300ms but we'll compromise.
01:12 Samir: ok that's helpful. sounds like you care a lot about consistent latency which is where Dedicated helps. quick question on data and isolation — do you require VPC/private deployment or is dedicated tenancy in Redwood hosted acceptable?
01:26 Maya: for now dedicated tenancy in our Redwood account is ok, but we do need network isolation and audit logs. long term we may look at VPC/private for regulated customers.
01:36 Roberto: must have SOC2, we also use HashiCorp Vault + AWS KMS, want to know key management options.
01:44 Lena: we support KMS integrations and customer-managed keys for Private, for Dedicated we have options to integrate with your KMS depending on deployment. i'll add docs.
01:53 Priya: on burst — our traffic is spiky, end of month settlements cause big bursts for a few hours, so can you support burst beyond reserved capacity?
02:04 Samir: yes, Dedicated supports burst capacity by borrowing from shared pools or autoscaling with warm standby; we can define burst policies — important to set SLOs for fallback.
02:14 Roberto: how predictable is cost when bursting? we can't have unexpected bills for business-critical flows.
02:20 Samir: we usually structure committed baseline + capped burst pricing with alerts; we can also set hard caps and circuit breakers so bursting won't exceed a fixed cost delta. we'll include examples in the pricing sheet.
02:31 Maya: technical deep-dive question — what GPUs do you run, and is model quantization supported? we plan to serve a mix of LLMs (open and some internal variants) and will need quantized pathways.
02:43 Lena: we support A100 and L40 variants for Dedicated, plus quantized execution paths (INT8/4) depending on model compat. kernel selection and KV cache handling is tuned per-model.
02:54 Roberto: any limits on model size? some of our internal models are 70B.
02:58 Lena: we can host up to 70B on multi-GPU shards; for very large models we recommend model slicing and our runtime supports KV cache sharding. i'll follow up with shard patterns.
03:09 Priya: what's the onboarding timeline — we have a pilot target in Q2.
03:13 Samir: typical pilot is 4-6 weeks: provisioning, baseline tests, tweaks. for Dedicated it's mostly provisioning GPUs and configuring autoscaling. if you sign a reserved commit we can prioritize capacity.
03:24 Maya: security checklist — SSO (SAML), RBAC, audit logs retention, data residency in us-east-1 and eu-west-1.
03:33 Lena: we support SAML SSO, RBAC with fine-grained roles, audit logs and can discuss retention periods. data residency is available via region pinning or Private.
03:43 Roberto: any customers using Dedicated for PCI-adjacent workloads?
03:47 Samir: yes we've got a few fintech customers using Dedicated with strict isolation and audit requirements. we'll share anonymized references.
03:55 Priya: competitors — we looked at OpenAI managed endpoints but cost and tenancy were concerns; Lambda Labs for on-prem but we need managed ops.
04:03 Samir: makes sense.
04:05 Lena: quick note — for predictable latency we recommend pinning a model variant and using prefix caching for the assistant flow; that reduces tail latency.
04:13 Maya: good to know.
04:15 Samir: ok recap/next steps: we'll send committed Dedicated pricing with burst tier options, SOC2 + integration docs, and a proposed 60-min technical deep dive for next week. lena will include benchmark notes and example throughput test plan.
04:30 Maya: sounds good — i'll also send a small workload sample for you to size nodes.
04:35 Samir: great, thanks everyone. we'll follow up with artifacts and calendar invite.

Action items (transcript):
- Samir: send pricing + capacity tiers (due 2026-03-29)
- Lena: attach benchmark notes and test plan (due 2026-03-30)
- Maya: provide workload profile and sample requests (due 2026-04-02)

End meeting.
